intent: Reduced kp gain from 10 to 8 to smooth steering control and decreased oscillation. Adjusted sensor x-positions outward by ±0.01 m to better cover sharp turns on the slalom track, aiming to reduce line loss events and improve finish rates. Maintained sensor size and forward y-positions to preserve early line detection benefits. Expect smoother control, fewer line losses, and improved slalom performance without compromising oval and s-bend results.
rationale: The previous iteration's increase in sensor size to 0.016 m and forward shift of sensor positions by +0.01 m improved line coverage and early detection, as expected, resulting in better progress and fewer line loss events on oval and s-bend tracks. However, the slalom track still shows zero finish rate, high line loss events (0.9), and elevated steering oscillation (0.398), indicating difficulty in handling sharp turns and control stability. Integration feedback suggests that if steering oscillation remains high, reducing kp and kd gains could smooth control. Also, adjusting sensor lateral positions by ±0.01 m might better cover sharp turns and improve finish rates on the slalom. Therefore, this iteration reduces kp from 10 to 8 to moderate control aggressiveness and shifts sensor x-coordinates outward by ±0.01 m to enhance lateral coverage of the line edges during sharp turns. Other geometry parameters remain unchanged to maintain stability and handling. The expected result is reduced steering oscillation, fewer line loss events, and improved finish rates on the slalom track, while maintaining strong performance on oval and s-bend tracks.
